nodes.label: SpinnakerCamera.open()
nodes.rationale: Must be idempotent because preflight opens the camera and leaves it open, then CaptureController.start() opens it again. Caches frame_rate from AcquisitionResultingFrameRate, not AcquisitionFrameRate, which is a ceiling (66.12 vs 199.93 on this camera).

nodes.label: SpinnakerCamera.load_user_set()
nodes.rationale: Checks PySpin.IsWritable() on the command node before executing and returns False with a clear log line rather than letting an AccessException escape; preflight, not the backend, decides whether a load failure blocks.

nodes.label: SpinnakerCamera.verify_settings()
nodes.rationale: Strictly read-only — never write a node to make a check pass, which is what keeps invariant 7 intact. An absent or unreadable node is a failed NodeCheck with actual '<unreadable>', not an exception. Float nodes compared as strings would be brittle, so the numeric frame-rate check is done separately by preflight against capture.fps_tolerance.

nodes.label: SpinnakerCamera.start_streaming()
nodes.rationale: Where invariant 3's 'not polling' is earned: subclass PySpin.ImageEventHandler and override OnImageEvent. Keep a reference to the handler on self — PySpin does not keep the Python object alive and a garbage-collected handler silently stops firing.

nodes.label: SpinnakerCamera.stop_streaming()
nodes.rationale: EndAcquisition() before UnregisterEventHandler() — the reverse order has caused crashes in past Spinnaker versions. Idempotent when not streaming.

nodes.label: SpinnakerCamera.close()
nodes.rationale: DeInit, del the CameraPtr, Clear the CameraList, then ReleaseInstance only at zero open cameras. Always tears down including on error paths so this app never becomes the thing that leaves the camera latched for the next run.

nodes.label: Shared PySpin System Singleton
nodes.rationale: System.GetInstance() is process-wide, so with N cameras each instance must share one System behind a reference-counted, lock-guarded module-level singleton. Releasing while another camera is open is a classic PySpin crash; CameraPtr and CameraList must be explicitly del'd before ReleaseInstance().

nodes.label: Copy GetNDArray() Before the Frame Escapes
nodes.rationale: GetNDArray() returns a view onto a buffer the SDK recycles at Release(); frames outlive the callback (pre-roll deque ~60, writer queue up to 120) so a view would alias data the camera already overwrote. Corruption scales with queue depth and looks like a compression artifact — the highest-risk line in the file.

nodes.label: Incomplete Frames Counted Separately From Dropped Frames
nodes.rationale: A full queue means the encoder cannot keep up; an incomplete image means the camera-to-host link dropped data. Different causes, different fixes, so they never share a counter — hence CameraBackend.incomplete_frame_count.

nodes.label: PySpin Exception Translation Convention
nodes.rationale: Every public method wraps PySpin calls and re-raises as CameraError so callers never import or catch PySpin-specific exceptions; `import PySpin` stays inside methods so the module remains importable with no SDK installed.
